blogs.title: "Idiopathic" Angioedema? Think Again.
blogs.description: Explores the critical diagnostic pitfall of pseudoangioedema in inflammatory myopathies. Discusses how dermatomyositis can present with neck swelling mimicking angioedema, the importance of recognizing atypical features that don't fit histaminergic or bradykinin-mediated angioedema, and practical tips for differentiating true angioedema from inflammatory mimics. A clinical reasoning piece on avoiding diagnostic momentum when the 'obvious' diagnosis doesn't quite fit.

blogs.title: Anti-SAE1: The DM Antibody You Can't Afford to Miss
blogs.description: An educational deep-dive into anti-SAE1 antibody dermatomyositis—a distinct clinical phenotype with characteristic features including high rates of dysphagia (46%), interstitial lung disease (43%), and malignancy association (18%). Discusses why recognizing this specific antibody matters for prognosis, counseling patients, and tailoring immunosuppression intensity. Includes practical guidance on when to order myositis antibody panels.

blogs.title: The CK Test: Diagnostic Gold in Atypical Presentations
blogs.description: Focuses on the pivotal role of creatine kinase testing in uncovering myositis when presentations are confusing. This case demonstrates how a single CK level (16,184 U/L) transformed the diagnostic trajectory. Discusses when CK should be ordered in the ED or acute setting, what constitutes a concerning elevation, and how 'liver function tests' that are actually AST/ALT from muscle can be an early clue to myopathy.

blogs.title: Dysphagia in Myositis: The Airway Complication That Defines Prognosis
blogs.description: Dedicated to dysphagia as both a presenting symptom and prognostic marker in dermatomyositis. Discusses the mechanism (pharyngeal muscle inflammation, cricopharyngeal dysfunction), clinical implications (aspiration pneumonitis risk, prolonged NG dependency), and why dysphagia should prompt aggressive multi-agent immunosuppression. Reviews swallow study findings and the multidisciplinary approach these patients require.

blogs.title: Dermatomyositis and Cancer: Who Needs What Screening?
blogs.description: Tackles the well-established malignancy association in dermatomyositis through a risk-stratified lens. Using this case (dermatomyositis + dysphagia + SAE1 positive + male = high risk) as a framework, reviews the IMACS guidelines for cancer screening. Discusses appropriate baseline workup (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, tumor markers, PET-CT, endoscopy), duration of surveillance, and how antibody type influences malignancy risk.
